goals: Explain employer demand and employee supply of labour
Calculate productivity, required hours, fte and labour costs per product with consistent units
Distinguish wage movement along demand from shifts due to other determinants; explain assumptions

priorTeaching: Book 2 §2.1.1, Gemiddelde totale kosten; manuscript lines 234–238
Book 2 §2.2.1, Rekenen met de oude waarde; manuscript lines 59–61
prerequisites.lessonSupport: Slide 3 revisits both procedures with separate MokStudio data; no assigned worked answers.

operations: 2a: reverse buyer/seller roles on labour market
prerequisites.priorTeaching: Not assumed. New in Book 4 §4.3.1 p. 114, definition and actor comparison.
prerequisites.startSupport: Overview explicitly labels 2 as exploration with theory p. 114; notes prompt using definition/figure, then return after slide 2 and before basis work.

operations: 3a,6a: read numeric w/L axes and quantities
3b,6b–d,7d: movement versus shift, ceteris paribus and simultaneous opposing effects
prerequisites.priorTeaching: Book 2 §2.2.1 explains ceteris paribus; preceding §4.2.7 teaches keeping periods and separate cases distinct, not labour-market roles.
prerequisites.lessonSupport: Slides 2 and 11–14 explicitly teach new actors, w and L, horizontal reading then vertical projection, movement, same-wage rightward shift, resets and unknown combined magnitude.

operations: 4b,7c: compare changes in numerator and denominator
prerequisites.priorTeaching: Average ratios from Book 2; labour productivity procedure is new here.
prerequisites.lessonSupport: Slides 4–10 teach units, fte, table-to-formula translation, reverse calculation, cost per product and production/productivity alternatives. Book pp. 115–118.

separateGraphModel.note: Graph comparisons are separate from the complete production plan. Qualitative combined-effects slide supplies no numerical order magnitude.

answerChecks.7c: Productivity and production both rise 37.5%; required hours stay 600. The universal claim is false.
answerChecks.7d: Higher wage only: movement to less labour along same demand. Extra exports only at fixed wage and technique: demand shifts right.

timing: Teacher guidance suggests two 55-minute lessons provisionally; no observed lesson-time or learning-effectiveness claim.
